note: The board's single data source. Rows carry states; TILE states are never stored — they derive at render by the pinned rule: a tile shows its most-blocking open row (to-clarify flag first, then waiting, then being built, then not reported, then not started; a tile whose rows are all unreported renders Not reported); a tile is done-and-checked only when every row is done. Milestones are rows of a milestone kind, in two classes: checked work, and observed world facts (source named). Vocabulary identical across prototype and shared versions; migration is a re-home of this file, not a re-entry of states. Schema v2 adds per-item watch targets and watch health; proposed changes live in board/proposals.json, never inside item states, and land only on a partner's tap. Standing requirement (Andy, 2026-10-24): the board surfaces things not documented yet — said on a call but never became an item · built but never claimed or recorded · decided but never written down — as proposed entries, which become items only on a partner's confirmation.

_stamp.derivation: Verbatim copy of the register, less the history log (history, history_notes, history_definition — withheld until the History view ships; the register is ahead of the extract there by standing decision) and less any internal field (rulings and one-side positions not yet jointly confirmed), plus a public-fit scrub (ruled 2026-10-26): call summaries withheld, the payments tile's detail generalized, the price block replaced by its partners-facing badge (the badge's status and note are the public form of the partners' shared position, not the register's internal state), org and repo paths replaced whole as values, and the partner's organization, company, and provider names generalized — the board's content is partner-private in substance and public only in the classes that fit a public page, plus this stamp. The snapshot line is generated by the derivation from the register's own counts. Selection: the component tree and the standing principles cross whole; tiles, gaps, and rows carry their component and node keys and, from schema 2.5, their guide fields (blocked_by and couples_with edges, kind_of_work, watch_tags, and the decision-time how). The board renders this data and nothing else.
